title: Principles of Roman Law
translator: Marguerite Wolff (from the German 'Prinzipien des römischen Rechts', 1934)
subject: Roman law
Legal history
Roman jurisprudence
Methodology of legal science
structure_note: A series of chapters, each devoted to one governing principle of Roman law. Two chapters are held: IV, 'Abstraction' (pp. 40-65), and VIII, 'Liberty' (pp. 140-163).

scan.format: PDF with an embedded text layer (OCR of a printed scan)
scan.page_numbering: Each fragment is a slice of the same scan and carries its own offset; fragment 1 starts at printed page 40, fragment 2 at printed page 140. The offset is recorded in each fragment manifest.
scan.quality_note: The embedded text layer is unproof-read OCR: ligatures, Latin words, italic footnote references and running heads are frequently mangled, and Greek comes through as noise. Corrections were applied only in the translations, not in text/.

coverage_note: Fragment 1 holds chapter IV ('Abstraction') complete, pp. 40-65, including the bilingual Latin/English reprint of D. 9. 2. 7. 1-8; 9 pr.-4; 11 pr.-5 on pp. 58-62. Fragment 2 holds chapter VIII ('Liberty') complete, pp. 140-163. Footnotes are held for both. No other chapter is in the library.

text_extraction.method: pypdf PdfReader.extract_text() over the PDF's own text layer
text_extraction.script: ad hoc; tools/ingest_fragment.py was not used because this PDF already carries a text layer

translations.conventions: Latin and Greek quotations and technical terms are left untranslated in their original form; square brackets inside Latin texts are Schulz's and mark passages he holds spurious. Bibliographic references in the footnotes keep their original form and abbreviations. Printed pagination is marked inline as [с. NN]. Obvious OCR defects in the source text layer were silently corrected against the sense (e.g. 'in hire civili' -> 'in iure civili', 'liber opcov' -> 'liber horon', 'maiores XXV minis' -> 'maiores XXV annis').

Same as the chapter IV translation. In addition, the Greek quotations in the footnotes (Aristot. Pol. 1317 b and 1310 a; Dio Cass. LVII. 8. 2; Soph. Antig. 737; Polyb. XXI. 22. 8) are unreadable in the source text layer and were restored from the passages Schulz cites; the file says so in its header. OCR defects corrected against the sense include 'frincefs' -> princeps, 'usucafio' -> usucapio, 'exceftio doli' -> exceptio doli, 'fietas' -> pietas, 'frovocatio' -> provocatio, 'civitates liberaes' -> civitates liberae.
